about: Input of scripts/build-console-credits.py: the facts chosen for each console's Credits & links, each with the source the script checks it against (see the script's docstring). `words` are the short phrases that prove a 'lead' fact (all of a group in one sentence of the article's lead); they are never shipped. `summary` and `role` are our own words. Chosen and checked 2026-10-23.

3do.summary: A design by The 3DO Company that other firms built and sold: Panasonic first, then GoldStar, Sanyo and Creative. An ARM60 runs it.

3ds.summary: Developed by Nintendo's research and engineering team and built by Nintendo and Foxconn. Two ARM processors and a DMP PICA200 graphics chip run it.

atari2600.summary: Atari's subsidiary Cyan Engineering built the prototype, codenamed Stella, after Nolan Bushnell went looking for a programmable home console. A MOS 6507 processor and the Television Interface Adaptor (TIA) run it.

people.name: Nolan Bushnell
people.role: Atari's CEO, who wanted a programmable home console

makers.name: Cyan Engineering
words: prototyped under the codename Stella by Atari subsidiary Cyan Engineering

atari7800.summary: Designed for Atari by General Computer Corporation; its MARIA chip draws arcade-style graphics, and it plays almost all 2600 cartridges.

atarijaguar.summary: Atari's last console, built for it by IBM. Two custom chips, Tom and Jerry, do the graphics and sound beside a Motorola 68000.

atarilynx.summary: Atari's colour handheld, developed at Epyx by Dave Needle and RJ Mical, two of the Amiga's designers.

colecovision.summary: Coleco's console, built around a Zilog Z80, a TMS9928A video chip and an SN76489 sound chip.

dreamcast.summary: Developed by a team under Hideki Sato, with a Hitachi SH-4, NEC's PowerVR2 graphics and a Yamaha sound chip. Sega's NAOMI arcade board is based on it.

people.name: Hideki Sato
people.role: Led the team that developed it

fds.summary: Nintendo's disk drive for the Famicom; its Ricoh 2C33 adds a wavetable sound channel.

gamecube.summary: Developed and made by Nintendo, with Foxconn also building it. IBM made its Gekko processor and ATI its Flipper graphics chip; the Triforce arcade board is based on it.

gamegear.summary: Sega's colour handheld, built around a Zilog Z80 and the Texas Instruments sound chip of the Master System. The Genesis Nomad came after it.

gb.summary: Nintendo R&D1 designed it under Gunpei Yokoi and Satoru Okada. Its Sharp SM83 processor carried on in the Game Boy Color and, for the older games, in the Game Boy Advance.

people.name: Gunpei Yokoi
people.role: Led the design team at Nintendo R&D1
words: under Gunpei Yokoi and Satoru Okada

people.name: Satoru Okada
people.role: Led the design with Yokoi; developed the Game Link Cable
words: under Gunpei Yokoi and Satoru Okada

gba.summary: Built by Nintendo's research and engineering team around an ARM7TDMI. The Game Boy's Sharp SM83 sits beside it, so the older cartridges still play.

gbc.summary: The Game Boy in colour, from Nintendo's research and engineering team. It keeps the Game Boy's Sharp SM83 processor and plays its cartridges.

intellivision.summary: Mattel's console, run on a General Instrument CP1600; INTV Corporation took it over in 1984.

mastersystem.summary: Sega's third-generation console, made by Sega and by Tectoy. A Zilog Z80 runs it; its Texas Instruments sound chip is the one of the SG-1000 and the Game Gear.

megadrive.summary: Designed by a Sega team under Hideki Sato and Masami Ishikawa. A Motorola 68000 and a Zilog Z80 run it; the sound comes from a Yamaha YM2612 and the SN76489 of the Master System.

people.name: Hideki Sato
words: supervised by Hideki Sato and Masami Ishikawa

people.name: Masami Ishikawa
words: supervised by Hideki Sato and Masami Ishikawa

n64.summary: Nintendo developed it with Silicon Graphics. NEC made its VR4300 processor and the Reality Coprocessor (RCP), which draws the picture.

nds.summary: Developed by Nintendo and built by Foxconn, with two ARM processors: an ARM946E-S, and the Game Boy Advance's ARM7TDMI.

neocd.summary: The Neo Geo on CD-ROM instead of cartridges, with the same Motorola 68000 as the cartridge console.

neogeo.summary: SNK's home console with the same hardware as its MVS arcade board: a Motorola 68000 runs the games, a Z80 the sound.

nes.summary: Designed by Masayuki Uemura, first as the Famicom, and developed by Nintendo R&D2. Ricoh made its 2A03 processor and the 2C02 picture chip.

people.name: Masayuki Uemura
words: The engineer Masayuki Uemura designed the 8-bit Famicom

ngpc.summary: SNK's colour handheld: a Toshiba TLCS-900/H runs the games and a Z80 the sound.

pcengine.summary: Made by NEC with Hudson Soft. The processor is Hudson Soft's HuC6280, the picture chips its HuC6270 and HuC6260.

pokemini.summary: Made by Nintendo with The Pokémon Company. A small Seiko Epson S1C88 processor runs the games.

ps2.summary: The PlayStation's successor, from Sony Computer Entertainment. Its Emotion Engine processor was developed with Toshiba; the Graphics Synthesizer draws the picture.

psp.summary: A handheld from Sony Computer Entertainment, with a processor based on the MIPS R4000. It came in several models, among them the PSP Go.

best_selling.title: Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories

psx.summary: Designed mainly by Ken Kutaragi and Sony Computer Entertainment in Japan, around an R3000 processor designed by MIPS Technologies. The PS one model followed.

saturn.summary: Sega's fifth-generation console, with two Hitachi SH-2 processors, two picture processors (VDP1 and VDP2) and a Yamaha sound chip.

sega32x.summary: Sega's add-on for the Mega Drive, with two SH-2 processors of its own; it was meant to carry players over to the Saturn.

segacd.summary: Sega's CD-ROM add-on for the Mega Drive. Its own Motorola 68000, faster than the Mega Drive's, runs the CD side, a custom ASIC scales and rotates graphics, and a Ricoh chip handles the sound.

sg-1000.summary: Made on the advice of Hayao Nakayama, then head of Sega in Japan. Texas Instruments made its picture and sound chips; the sound chip returned in the Master System and the Game Gear.

people.name: Hayao Nakayama
people.role: Head of Sega in Japan; it was made on his advice
words: on the advice of Hayao Nakayama

snes.summary: Designed by Masayuki Uemura and developed by Nintendo R&D2. Ricoh made its 5A22 processor and the picture chips; the sound runs on Nintendo's S-SMP.

people.name: Masayuki Uemura
words: Masayuki Uemura, a Nintendo engineer, designed the 16-bit SNES

best_selling.title: Street Fighter II: The World Warrior

supergrafx.summary: Made by NEC Home Electronics. It has the PC Engine's HuC6280A processor, with two HuC6270 picture chips and a HuC6202 to blend them.

chips.name: Hudson Soft HuC6270 (VDC), two of them

vectrex.summary: Conceived by John Ross at Smith Engineering as a handheld; it became a tabletop console with its own vector screen.

virtualboy.summary: Made at Nintendo R&D1 under Gunpei Yokoi; an NEC V810 drives its red 3D display.

people.name: Gunpei Yokoi
people.role: Led its development as general manager of Nintendo R&D1

wii.summary: Shigeru Miyamoto and Genyo Takeda led its development. IBM made the Broadway processor; the graphics chip is ATI's Hollywood.

people.name: Shigeru Miyamoto
people.role: Led its development, with Genyo Takeda
words: Shigeru Miyamoto and Genyo Takeda led development

people.name: Genyo Takeda
people.role: Led its development, with Shigeru Miyamoto
words: Shigeru Miyamoto and Genyo Takeda led development

wonderswan.summary: Bandai's handheld, developed with Gunpei Yokoi's company Koto Laboratory; it was the last hardware he worked on. An NEC V30 MZ runs it.

people.name: Gunpei Yokoi
people.role: Developed it with Bandai through his company, Koto Laboratory; his last hardware
words: final piece of hardware Yokoi worked on
